1.title: Data Catalogs
1.text: Welcome to Module seven: Data Catalogs. This module covers the task statement: understand data cataloging systems. Each part of this module comes from the study notes of the same name, so you can read the notes after you watch.

1.title: What You Will Learn
1.text: By the end of this module you will be able to do six things. Explain what a data catalog is and why query engines need one. Build and reference a technical catalog: the A W S Glue Data Catalog and an Apache Hive metastore. Discover schemas and populate the catalog with A W S Glue crawlers. Synchronize partitions with the catalog. Create connections for cataloging. Create and manage a business data catalog in Amazon SageMaker Catalog.

1.title: Case Check-In: Kestrel Freight Finds Its Data
1.text: Our running case is Kestrel Freight. Kestrel Freight Finds Its Data. New order files appear in S three every day in new folders. Analysts cannot tell which table is the real one or what a column means. Athena, Glue and E M R (Elastic MapReduce) must all see the same tables. Your job: build one technical catalog for the engines and one business catalog for the people.

1.title: What a Catalog Is and Why It Matters
1.text: What a Catalog Is and Why It Matters. The figure shows this: The catalog is the map: the A W S Glue Data Catalog holds database, table, schema and partition metadata, and Athena, Redshift Spectrum, E M R and Glue use it to find and read the data in S three. A data catalog is a central store of metadata (data about data): where the data is, its format and schema, its partitions, and often what it means and who owns it. Technical catalog: for engines and engineers: databases, tables, columns and types, partitions, locations, formats.

1.title: What a Catalog Is and Why It Matters, continued
1.text: What a Catalog Is and Why It Matters, continued. Business catalog: for people: business terms, descriptions, owners, data products, and access requests. Schema-on-read: the data stays in S three as files; the catalog tells engines how to read them.

1.title: What a Catalog Is and Why It Matters, continued
1.text: What a Catalog Is and Why It Matters, continued. What. A W S Glue Data Catalog: Managed, serverless central metadata repository, Hive metastore compatible. Apache Hive metastore: The open-source metadata service of the Hadoop world. Used by. A W S Glue Data Catalog: Athena, Redshift Spectrum, E M R, Glue, Lake Formation, SageMaker. Apache Hive metastore: Spark, Hive, Presto on self-managed or E M R clusters. Choose it when. A W S Glue Data Catalog: You want one managed catalog for all A W S analytics. Apache Hive metastore: You already run a Hive metastore (you can point E M R at the Glue Data Catalog instead to remove the metastore to manage). Glue Data Catalog parts: databases (containers of tables), tables (schema, location, format, partition keys), partitions, connections, crawlers, classifiers and schema registries for streaming schemas.

1.title: What a Catalog Is and Why It Matters, continued
1.text: What a Catalog Is and Why It Matters, continued. Use a catalog to consume data from its source: query by table name in Athena (select... from sales.orders) and in Glue jobs (from catalog), instead of hard-coding S three paths and schemas. Lake Formation adds permissions on catalog databases and tables (Module fifteen). Exam tip: "Athena, E M R and Glue must share table definitions" to the A W S Glue Data Catalog (set it as the Hive metastore for E M R).

1.title: Glue Crawlers: Discovering Schemas
1.text: Glue Crawlers: Discovering Schemas. The figure shows this: How a Glue crawler works: connect to the data store, classify the data to infer the schema, group it into tables and partitions, and write metadata to the Data Catalog. A crawler scans a data store, infers the format and schema, and creates or updates tables and partitions in the Data Catalog.

1.title: Glue Crawlers: Discovering Schemas, continued
1.text: Glue Crawlers: Discovering Schemas, continued. Steps: run custom classifiers in order (the first match wins), else built-in classifiers (Jason, C S V, Avro, Parquet, O R C (Optimized Row Columnar) and more); connect to the store; infer the schema; write metadata; each table gets a classification label. Data stores: S three, J D B C (Java Database Connectivity) databases (R D S, Aurora, Redshift and others), DynamoDB, MongoDB and DocumentDB, Delta, Iceberg and Hudi tables, and more. Schedule a crawler (on demand, cron, or on an event) so new files, columns and partitions are found; a Glue trigger starts at most two crawlers.

1.title: Glue Crawlers: Discovering Schemas, continued
1.text: Glue Crawlers: Discovering Schemas, continued. Partitions: when most folders at a level have similar schemas, the crawler makes partitions (year equals two thousand twenty-six or month equals eleven or ) of one table; to make separate tables, give each table root its own include path. Update behavior: choose what happens when the schema changes (update the table definition or ignore) and when objects disappear (delete from the catalog, mark as deprecated, or ignore). Athena tip: in Athena one table equals one S three prefix; objects with different schemas under one prefix can give empty results: separate include paths. Exam tip: "New daily folders appear and the table must pick up the new partitions and columns automatically" to a scheduled (or event-driven) Glue crawler.

1.title: Synchronizing Partitions
1.text: Synchronizing Partitions. Partitions split a table by key values so queries read only the needed folders; the catalog must know each partition before engines can use it. Hive-style layout: S three or or bucket or sales or year equals two thousand twenty-six or month equals eleven or day equals seven or (key equals value in the path).

1.title: Synchronizing Partitions, continued
1.text: Synchronizing Partitions, continued. Glue crawler (scheduled or event-driven). Easy, automatic; also detects schema changes. Athena M S C K repair table. Hive-style paths (lowercase key names, S three or or locations) are in S three but missing from the table. Athena alter table add partition. Non-Hive layout (for example two thousand twenty-six or eleven or seven or ) or a single known partition; use if not exists. Glue A P I BatchCreatePartition or a job writing with partition updates. Pipelines that create partitions as they write. Partition projection (Athena). Highly partitioned, predictable layouts: Athena computes partitions from table properties instead of looking them up, so no sync is needed and queries are faster.

1.title: Synchronizing Partitions, continued
1.text: Synchronizing Partitions, continued. Partition indexes (Glue). Tables with very many partitions: faster partition lookup (Athena cannot read more than one million partitions in one scan). Keep each table in its own folder hierarchy, or M S C K repair table can attach partitions of one table to another. Exam tip: "Hundreds of thousands of date partitions make Athena planning slow" to partition projection or partition indexes. "Firehose writes two thousand twenty-six or eleven or seven or folders" (non-Hive) to alter table add partition or partition projection.

2.title: Connections for Cataloging
2.text: Connections for Cataloging. A Glue connection stores how to reach a data store: type (J D B C, MongoDB, Kafka, Salesforce and more), host and port, credentials (use A W S Secrets Manager), S S L (Secure Sockets Layer) settings, and the V P C (Virtual Private Cloud), subnet and security groups if the store is private. Use a connection in a crawler (to catalog a J D B C table), in a job (read and write) or for Kafka sources. Network rules: security groups must allow the Glue connection to reach the store; for stores outside A W S use a N A T (network address translation) gateway path; a job can use J D B C connections in one subnet.

2.title: Connections for Cataloging, continued
2.text: Connections for Cataloging, continued. New source or target connection: create the connection, test it, attach it to a crawler or job, and crawl to catalog the tables. Keep credentials out of the console fields: reference a secret. Exam tip: "A crawler cannot reach a private R D S (Relational Database Service) database" to check the connection's V P C, subnet and security group, and that the secret is valid.

2.title: Business Data Catalogs: Amazon SageMaker Catalog
2.text: Business Data Catalogs: Amazon SageMaker Catalog. Amazon SageMaker Catalog is the business data catalog of Amazon SageMaker Unified Studio: it helps people discover, understand, govern and share data and A I (artificial intelligence) assets. This fact moves with the A W S pages, so check the current value before you rely on it.

2.title: Business Data Catalogs: Amazon SageMaker Catalog, continued
2.text: Business Data Catalogs: Amazon SageMaker Catalog, continued. It builds on the technical metadata (for example tables in the Glue Data Catalog) and adds a business layer:; Assets: the datasets and resources that are published to the catalog; Business glossary: shared business terms with one meaning (for example "delivered order"); Metadata forms: custom fields (owner, sensitivity, refresh rate) attached to assets; Data products: groups of related assets packaged for consumers; Publish and subscribe: producers publish; consumers search and request a subscription; the owner approves, and access is granted. This fact moves with the A W S pages, so check the current value before you rely on it.

2.title: Business Data Catalogs: Amazon SageMaker Catalog, continued
2.text: Business Data Catalogs: Amazon SageMaker Catalog, continued. It works inside domains, domain units and projects (Module fourteen), which organize teams and control who can see and use what. Lineage (Module nine) and access (Module eighteen) are managed through the same catalog. Audience. Glue Data Catalog: Engines and engineers. SageMaker Catalog: Analysts, data owners and stewards. Content. Glue Data Catalog: Schemas, partitions, locations. SageMaker Catalog: Glossary, descriptions, owners, data products, subscriptions. Question it answers. Glue Data Catalog: "How do I read this?". SageMaker Catalog: "What is this, who owns it, may I use it?". Exam tip: "Analysts need to search, understand and request access to datasets with business terms" to Amazon SageMaker Catalog (a business catalog). "The engine needs schemas and partitions" to Glue Data Catalog (a technical catalog). This fact moves with the A W S pages, so check the current value before you rely on it.

2.title: Module Recap
2.text: Here is the recap. Catalog: Metadata about data: location, schema, partitions, meaning; technical (engines) versus business (people). Glue Data Catalog: Managed, Hive-compatible; databases, tables, partitions, connections; shared by Athena, E M R, Spectrum, Glue, Lake Formation. Hive metastore: Open-source; E M R can use the Glue Data Catalog instead. Crawler: Classifiers (custom first, then built-in) to infer schema to tables and partitions; scheduled. Partitions: Hive-style key equals value; sync by crawler, M S C K repair table, alter table add partition, A P I. Connections: Type, host, secret (Secrets Manager), S S L, V P C or subnet or security groups; used by crawlers and jobs. SageMaker Catalog: Business catalog: assets, glossary, metadata forms, data products, publish or subscribe with approval.

2.title: Practice Question 1
2.text: Question one. New dated folders (year equals two thousand twenty-six or month equals eleven or day equals eight) arrive in S three daily with occasional new columns. The table in the Data Catalog must update automatically. Which solution fits best? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C. A scheduled crawler discovers new partitions and schema changes and updates the table.

2.title: Practice Question 2
2.text: Question two. Select two. Data is stored under Hive-style paths such as year equals two thousand twenty-six or month equals eleven or and a new partition is missing from an Athena table. Which two actions add it? The five options are on the screen. The answers are B and E. M S C K repair table loads Hive-style partitions into the table, and a crawler also discovers them. The other actions do not register partitions.

2.title: Practice Question 3
2.text: Question three. An Athena table has several hundred thousand date partitions and query planning is slow. The partition layout is predictable. What is the best improvement? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B. Partition projection computes partition values and locations from table properties instead of reading them from the catalog, which speeds up planning for predictable layouts.

2.title: Practice Question 4
2.text: Question four. A crawler must catalog tables in a private Amazon R D S for PostgreSQL database. Which item is R E Q U I R E D for the crawler to connect? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A. A Glue connection holds how to reach the data store, including network settings and credentials, which the crawler uses to connect.

2.title: Practice Question 5
2.text: Question five. Business analysts want to search for datasets using business terms, see who owns them and request access, with owner approval. Which service feature fits best? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A. SageMaker Catalog is a business catalog with glossary terms, data products and a publish and subscribe workflow with approval, built on top of technical metadata.

2.title: Answers at a Glance
2.text: Here are all five answers. Question one: C. Question two: B and E. Question three: B. Question four: A. Question five: A. In the next module, we continue the course.
